source.title: Merging Feed-Forward Sublayers for Compressed Transformers
source.authors: Neha Verma; Kenton Murray; Kevin Duh

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether adjacent feed-forward sublayers can be aligned and merged with little downstream-performance loss. This is a within-model layer setting, not a test of cross-model convergence.
record.gate_note: The study reports permutation-aligned FF merges and downstream task scores, which bear on V4's layer-mapping/interchangeability aspect. Its CKA measurements compare FF layers within each model, not independently trained models. No scale sweep, cross-modal image-caption alignment, or comparison of similarity metrics is reported. CKA findings are recorded under fits_no_version because within-model layer similarity does not test the claim versions as phrased.
record.test_reason: The study uses permutation alignment associated with convergent learning to compress individual Transformers. It measures within-model FF-layer similarity and compression performance, not alignment or interchangeability between different models. V4 explicitly concerns mapping one model's representations onto another's; merging layers within one model does not test it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that aligning, merging, and tying adjacent FF sublayers, followed by recovery fine-tuning, provides effective Transformer compression across tasks and can combine with quantization or QLoRA. They suggest that within-model FF activation similarity may help explain mergeability; they do not establish cross-model convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study aligns neurons across adjacent FF sublayers within one model using activation cross-correlation and an assignment algorithm, then averages and ties weights for compression. It does not test cross-model representation convergence or convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report different pre-tuning outcomes by selected layer window, reduced differences after recovery fine-tuning, similar results across anchor locations, and stronger permutation-based results than vanilla merging, especially at larger merge amounts.

fits_no_version.finding: After recovery fine-tuning, permutation-aligned FF merging retains substantial task performance within individual Transformers. At one-third removal, ViT accuracy is 79.2 versus 80.3, GPT-2 perplexity is 17.27 versus 16.16, and translation BLEU is 33.5 versus 35.8. Larger merges incur greater losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adjacent FF parameter sets within a pretrained Transformer can be aligned, averaged, and tied for compression, with task performance partly recovered by fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Compression performance varies little across the tested anchor choices and becomes similar across selected layer windows after recovery fine-tuning; permutation alignment generally improves on vanilla merging.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested within-model FF compression procedure benefits from permutation alignment and is relatively robust to anchor and layer-window choices after recovery tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: OLMo FF merging followed by QLoRA yields SamSum ROUGE scores of 51.61, 26.95, and 47.41 versus unmerged QLoRA scores of 53.68, 29.34, and 49.83.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model FF compression can be combined with QLoRA while retaining substantial downstream summarization performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report regions of high CKA similarity between FF outputs within each tested model, with no comparable pattern in attention outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some FF sublayers within an individual Transformer produce similar activations even when isolated from residual additions.

record.problems: The CKA results are presented as plots without numerical values in the text. The study measures within-model layer similarity rather than cross-model alignment, and evaluates the method on a limited set of Transformer models and tasks.

untested.parts: Increasing alignment across independently trained models as size or capability increases.
Alignment of paired image-caption representations across vision and language models, and its relationship to capability.
Shared features or subspaces across networks trained from different initializations.
All cross-model representation mapping and interchangeability. Within-model parameter averaging, tying, and recovery tuning do not test this version.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.
Dependence of measured cross-model convergence on metrics, metric settings, or input distribution.
Incomplete or plateauing cross-model alignment and explanations involving shared training data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: All cannot_determine states refer to the supplied claim versions, not uncertainty about the reported task scores. The record's V4 verdicts incorrectly broaden cross-model interchangeability to within-model compression. No additional results bearing on the supplied versions require missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no comparison of representations across independently trained models.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations.

Tests permutation alignment and merging of adjacent FF sublayers within a model, not mappings between independently trained models, stitching across models, relative representations, or unpaired-data mappings.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs for convergence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain cross-model alignment, or whether cross-model alignment plateaus.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Permutation-aligned FF merges at 1/3 removal in ViT and GPT-2, and anchor-choice comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Performance is near the reported uncompressed reference for ViT and GPT-2 at 1/3 removal (r01, r04), and changes little across anchor locations (r31-r39). This supports a limited within-model FF-layer interchangeability result.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: More extensive FF merging, translation and QLoRA summarization settings, and alternate layer selections
reader_labels.reason: The losses are more substantial at 1/2 and especially near-total FF removal, and results vary across tasks and selected layer groups (r02-r03, r05-r09, r20-r30, r41, r43, r45). These results qualify the extent and setting of the within-model mergeability finding.
